label: Youssef Ahmed
bio: Computer Science & Statistics student at UBC. I build data and AI tooling — benchmarking platforms for schools, infrastructure that provisions itself, and the occasional automation that saves someone an afternoon.

children.label: Developed a Python platform that analyzes and benchmarks student performance across grades, schools, and national datasets, including automated scale score calculations and statistical comparisons
Automated client-ready school reports (charts, comparisons, executive summaries) for non-technical stakeholders
Provisioning AWS infrastructure with Terraform (Infrastructure as Code) to support a hosted deployment across schools throughout the Middle East, serving thousands of students
Translated how organizations operate (their people, assets, documents, operations, events, commitments, and transactions) into a universal ontology that serves as a structured context layer for AI
Developed a framework with formal, reusable definitions enabling AI to understand organizational structure, relationships, and processes across different companies and industries
Visited industrial sites across Egypt and the UAE to document operational issues and planned automation
Researched multi-view 3D reconstruction methods for a proposed multi-camera rig that scans parts as they move
Developed a Java desktop application with a Swing GUI and console UI backed by the same model, supporting vehicle check-in, slot allocation, retrieval, and real-time wait time estimation
Achieved high JUnit 5 test coverage across model and persistence layers and documented the architecture in UML
Built an event-driven n8n workflow that updates vehicle records in Supabase as cars enter or leave
Automated an HR intake process: the workflow monitors incoming emails for resumes, transforms them into structured candidate records, and screens applications against specified selection criteria

Co-built CrowdCost with a 5-person team: a Next.js/TypeScript and FastAPI console that flags transit surges at UBC, Waterfront, and Park Royal 1 hour ahead (82% caught in a backtest) and recommends moving spare buses

Built a 9-task Databricks pipeline in PySpark and SQL over 21.5M cell-tower pings and TransLink data that cleaned the data our surge model trained on, plus a LightGBM forecaster (MLflow) and a SciPy bus optimizer
Placed 4th after pitching a live demo to judges from TransLink, PwC, Databricks, Rogers, West Vancouver, and UBC

Modeled ICU-transfer risk from the first 8 hours of an admission with a 9-person team from pharmacy, medicine, and data science, using 22,000+ de-identified St. Michael's Hospital inpatient encounters
Co-built the XGBoost model (ROC-AUC 0.743) in a secure research environment, after the team widened scope to all general internal medicine patients because stroke and 24-hour subsets were too small

Placed 14th of 49 teams (team of 4) on a real-world problem set by Amazon Robotics engineers: routing warehouse robots that carry inventory pods to pick stations, scored on delivery speed across hidden test cases

Benchmarked multiple routing strategies in pure Python and shipped a congestion-aware Dijkstra planner that predicts when busy aisles clear, with greedy robot-to-pod assignment, batched pickups, and dock clearing
